name: Velo3D, Inc.
subcategory: laser powder-bed fusion (L-PBF) metal printers and contract production (Sapphire)
origin_detail: Venture-backed startup founded in 2014 ('Since our founding in 2014') and led at its 2021 listing by CEO Benny Buller; went public on 2021-09-29 by merging with JAWS Spitfire Acquisition Corp, a SPAC incorporated 2020-09-11. Since the December 2024 debt-for-equity exchange it has been controlled by Arrayed Notes Acquisition Corp (parent Arrayed Additive), whose CEO Arun Jeldi became Velo3D's CEO. HQ Fremont, CA.
flagship_projects: Sapphire / Sapphire XC / Sapphire XC 1MZ L-PBF printers
openness_notes: Closed: the 10-Ks describe 'proprietary laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) technology', 'Flow is a highly advanced and proprietary software platform', and the 'proprietary Intelligent Fusion manufacturing process', protected by 57 issued patents (45 US) as of the FY2025 10-K. Materials are supplied as vendor 'recipes' (16 metals by 2025). No open designs, firmware or parameter sets found. 0 at both dates.

license_history.license: Proprietary (Sapphire hardware, Flow and Assure software, Intelligent Fusion process)

exit_events.note: Business combination closed 2021-09-29; $155M PIPE (15.5M shares at $10.00), earn-out of up to 21,758,148 shares; NYSE: VLD. Implied equity value not found in fetched pages; StockAnalysis gives a $1.43B market cap at 2021-12-31.

Change of control while the stock stayed public: on 2024-12-24 Arrayed exchanged $22.4M of secured notes (+$0.4M interest) for 185,151,333 new shares, giving it 95% of the company; six directors including Buller resigned; the remaining shares kept trading on OTCQX.

risk_events: Customer concentration: SpaceX was 41.1% of 2020 and 27.8% of 2021 revenue; top three customers 62.0% (2021), 47.0% (2024), 33.2% (2025)
Dec 2023: $18M registered direct offering; 1-for-35 reverse split (2024-06-13) and 1-for-15 reverse split (2025-07-28)
Sept 2024: NYSE delisting notice (8-K Item 3.01, 2024-09-12); the stock (ticker VLD) moved to OTCQX, later OTC Pink (VLDX)
Dec 2024: debt-for-equity exchange gave Arrayed Notes Acquisition Corp. 95% of the stock; Arrayed CEO Arun Jeldi became CEO
Aug 2025: relisted on the Nasdaq Capital Market as VELO (2025-08-19) with a $20.1M offering at $3.00 per share
FY2025 10-K: 'substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern'; 2025 net loss $71.4M on $46.0M revenue
Nov 2026: positive EBITDA target pushed from 2H 2026 to 2028; capex guidance cut from $40-50M to $10-20M
robustness: Fragile: a going-concern warning, recurring losses, two reverse splits and a controlling shareholder (Arrayed held 95% after the exchange; Jeldi beneficially owned ~48.6% by March 2026). Customers depend on proprietary Flow/Assure software and vendor-qualified recipes, so there is no open fallback. Partial offsets: growing defense-led revenue (Q3 2026 $20.5M, about +50% y/y from $13.6M), $75.7M cash and a $40.1M backlog at 2026-09-30, and a five-year Sandia CRADA (Nov 2026).
physical_science_relevance: Directly relevant as a closed L-PBF platform: Sapphire printers make support-free metal parts in aluminium, titanium, nickel superalloys and copper alloys from 16 vendor-developed 'recipes' (2025). Parameters live in proprietary Flow software, so alloy-development work (new Al compositions, scan-strategy exploration, data for self-driving labs) is constrained compared with open-parameter research machines such as Aconity3D's. The 2026 Sandia CRADA and Arrayed's 'lightweight magnesium and aluminum alloy' manufacturing show the company moving toward defense production rather than research tooling.
openness_effect_assessment: Velo3D stayed fully proprietary and sold support-free L-PBF as a differentiated, patent-protected process; that won SpaceX and aerospace customers but not a sustainable business at SPAC-era expectations. The collapse (a market cap of $1.43B to about $0.1B, delisting, debt-for-equity control by Arrayed) came from losses, customer concentration and cash needs; openness played no visible role either way.
key_takeaway: Velo3D is the third 2021 metal-AM SPAC and the one that survived by being recapitalised rather than sold: after its value fell more than 90%, a creditor took 95% of the equity in 2024, and it relisted on Nasdaq in 2025 as a defense-focused producer with a going-concern warning. For an LPBF alloy lab it is the archetype of the closed, recipe-locked production printer, good at qualified parts and poor as an open research instrument.
